access.edition_or_version: Urdu letters, 19th century; English via Daud Rahbar (Dev Publishers, 2022)

mechanics.reader_promise: Talk-like companionship across distance: the letter as a substitute for conversation with a friend.
mechanics.point_of_view: First-person epistolary address to named friends and acquaintances, often beginning informally.
mechanics.psychic_distance: Close and equal: the addressee is treated as a confidant capable of sharing a joke.
mechanics.dialogue: Conversational diction and humour; the letter 'talks' as if spoken rather than performed.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Rejected the formal mursala convention; easy, simple, conversational Urdu prose; humour and self-deprecation; aspiration to write lines the reader will enjoy.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Episodic and associative, accumulating relationship across many letters rather than building a single arc.
mechanics.tone_markers: Informal opening, conversational register, humour, equality with the addressee, pleasure-oriented address.
